notes.content: History is one of the broadest and most universal of the humanities. Just as the personalities of individuals are shaped through the totality of their past experiences, so cultures and institutions also develop in time. The study of history can help students understand themselves and their culture better and develop a more tolerant and humane spirit toward others. In this way, as in so many others, a knowledge of the past can help all of us meet the problems of today with greater understanding and compassion.The Bachelor of Arts degree program in History at California State University, Fresno offers undergraduate students seminars on a wide range of historical periods and approaches. The program also provides the conscientious student with the requisite research skills to ensure success in future academic or related pursuits. The History Department at California State University, Fresno is especially strong in the areas of Ancient History, Modern European History, United States History, Latin American History, and Military History. There are lower-division history courses that are used to meet an area of major requirements, but many of these courses are not articulated. These courses must be taken at Fresno State after transfer. The course options can be found in the General Catalog here . Advising Notes History majors are not permitted to take history courses by CR/NC grading. A grade of C or higher is required for all courses to be counted toward the major. It is strongly recommended that history majors take both HIST 11 and HIST 12. Students who are planning to do graduate work in history are advised to take a foreign language and HIST 196 as an undergraduate in consultation with the History Department. In addition to the major program requirements, every student must also complete the University’s baccalaureate degree requirements such as: American Government and Institutions ( PLSI 2 ) General Education Requirements (43 units) Additional University Graduation Requirements (9 units) - Students with a declared History major following a TMC/ADT similar pathway are exempt from 6 units of this degree requirement. Upper-Division Writing Requirement General Education, Additional University Graduation Requirements, and Upper-division Writing courses can be double counted with major requirements. These courses include HIST 20 or HIST 21 (Area 4B) and HIST 100W . See advisor for details. Sufficient Elective Units to Meet Required Total Units (varies); it is recommended that units in this area be utilized to complete a second major or minor. A full description of the University’s graduation requirements can be found in the Baccalaureate Degree Requirements .

History is one of the broadest and most universal of the humanities. Just as the personalities of individuals are shaped through the totality of their past experiences, so cultures and institutions also develop in time. The study of history can help students understand themselves and their culture better and develop a more tolerant and humane spirit toward others. In this way, as in so many others, a knowledge of the past can help all of us meet the problems of today with greater understanding and compassion.The Bachelor of Arts degree program in History at California State University, Fresno offers undergraduate students seminars on a wide range of historical periods and approaches. The program also provides the conscientious student with the requisite research skills to ensure success in future academic or related pursuits. The History Department at California State University, Fresno is especially strong in the areas of Ancient History, Modern European History, United States History, Latin American History, and Military History.


﻿There are lower-division history courses that are used to meet an area of major requirements, but many of these courses are not articulated. These courses must be taken at Fresno State after transfer. The course options can be found in the General Catalog here.


Advising Notes

History majors are not permitted to take history courses by CR/NC grading.

A grade of C or higher is required for all courses to be counted toward the major.

It is strongly recommended that history majors take both HIST 11 and HIST 12.

  • Students who are planning to do graduate work in history are advised to take a foreign language and HIST 196 as an undergraduate in consultation with the History Department.


In addition to the major program requirements, every student must also complete the University’s baccalaureate degree requirements such as:

  • American Government and Institutions (PLSI 2)
  • General Education Requirements (43 units)
  • Additional University Graduation Requirements (9 units) - Students with a declared History major following a TMC/ADT similar pathway are exempt from 6 units of this degree requirement.
  • Upper-Division Writing Requirement
  • General Education, Additional University Graduation Requirements, and Upper-division Writing courses can be double counted with major requirements. These courses include HIST 20 or HIST 21 (Area 4B) and HIST 100W. See advisor for details.
  • Sufficient Elective Units to Meet Required Total Units (varies); it is recommended that units in this area be utilized to complete a second major or minor.

A full description of the University’s graduation requirements can be found in the Baccalaureate Degree Requirements.

notes.content: Additional University Graduation Requirements The Additional University Graduation Requirements are designed to complement the GE requirements. It is the policy of Fresno State, that all students will cultivate and refine their affective, cognitive, and physical faculties through studying great works of the human imagination; be equipped for lifelong understanding and development of themselves as integrated physiological, social, and psychological beings; and be prepared to understand and live in a multicultural and international world through their undergraduate education. This will be accomplished through a total of 9 units from the following areas, each requiring 3 units: Arts/Humanities (A/H) - All students are required to take an Arts/Humanities course to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. Lifelong-Understanding and Self-Development (L/S) - All students are required to take a lifelong understanding and self-development course to for graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. Multicultural/International (M/I) - All Students are required to take a Multicultural / International course at Fresno State to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level.
notes.contentHtml:
Additional University Graduation Requirements


The Additional University Graduation Requirements are designed to complement the GE requirements. It is the policy of Fresno State, that all students will cultivate and refine their affective, cognitive, and physical faculties through studying great works of the human imagination; be equipped for lifelong understanding and development of themselves as integrated physiological, social, and psychological beings; and be prepared to understand and live in a multicultural and international world through their undergraduate education.

This will be accomplished through a total of 9 units from the following areas, each requiring 3 units:

  1. Arts/Humanities (A/H) - All students are required to take an Arts/Humanities course to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  2. Lifelong-Understanding and Self-Development (L/S) - All students are required to take a lifelong understanding and self-development course to for graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  3. Multicultural/International (M/I) - All Students are required to take a Multicultural / International course at Fresno State to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level.
